text: Our class, as I was saying, we have now eight signals in our constellation, so they are close to each other. So what is the observation, farther observation that we can make in this case? The fact is that when our radio interface transmits toward the base station, as we said, the signal goes through the air, and while traveling, it may be affected, as we will discuss later, by several different phenomena. Just an example: if it rains or it's foggy, the signal will bump into these smaller water particles that are in the air, and that causes some problems to our signal. The signal will get weaker. So as the signal travels through the air, there are several different issues: obstacles, atmosphere, particles, etc. That essentially causes a reduction in the power of the signal itself. So it travels, it's like getting tired to reach the destination. So it arrives at the destination with a lower level of power than what it was transmitted with. And also while traveling, it may collect. Let's say, I mean, it can travel. It may meet other.
